cohort: 559 nulliparous women who delivered a neonate weighing >4000 g between 2008 and 2012
finding: Women who underwent elective cesarean section for macrosomic infants reported higher satisfaction with childbirth compared to those who attempted vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Women who underwent elective cesarean section were more likely to be satisfied with childbirth than those who attempted a vaginal delivery, including those who had an emergency cesarean during labor.
